title: Unit 7 Stand-alone 4: Alzheimer's Disease Family Teaching (Agitation)

question.stem: Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the teaching? Select all that apply.
question.preamble: The nurse is teaching the family member of a client with moderate Alzheimer's disease (AD).

options.text: Use distraction when the client becomes agitated.
Place calendars within clear view of the client.
Use short, simple sentences and provide step-by-step instructions for the client.
Avoid reminiscing with the client about past experiences in order to avoid feelings of loss and loneliness.
Encourage the client to participate in a daytime exercise program to promote restful sleep at night.

question.explanation: Distraction (Option 1) is a standard de-escalation technique for agitation in AD. Calendars (Option 2) support reality orientation. Short, simple sentences with step-by-step instructions (Option 3) match the client's cognitive processing ability. A daytime exercise program (Option 5) helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle and can reduce sundowning and improve nighttime rest. Reminiscence about long-term memories (Option 4) should be encouraged, not avoided, since long-term memory is often preserved in AD and reminiscing is a validating, anxiety-reducing activity.
